title: dotlineform
content_html:
dotlineform is an ongoing project consisting of a portfolio of visual artwork, a collection of texts and a library of research and conceptual writing.

The portfolio, texts and library are different ways of asking questions. Some works are deliberately abstract or difficult to read, others begin with something so ordinary it might pass unnoticed. Some of the writing in the library looks to evolution to ask why we seek patterns and why we need things to mean something. An account of where that impulse comes from opens another question about what we do with it.

Much of the work derives from a precept~belief that there exists fundamental Platonic Forms that shape nature and that whilst these forms cannot be perceived directly, their efficacy can be felt when we observe the world around and inside us. Spontaneous and chance events reveal the underlying emptiness of our perceptions and the interdependences between all objects and events in our environment; the duality of meaning and meaning-less, truth and not-truth, is the basis for the ongoing photographic project which de-contextualises often random or mundane moments from a personal photographic archive.

Quantum mechanics is of interest here because its abstract language describes things outside of conventional comprehension, yet these models are precise enough to guide the design of real machines. A mathematical model can work in that very concrete sense and still leave us asking what it means or tells us about 'reality'.
